description: Known gaps in the TARA catalog, computed from the registrar. Published rather than hidden so that any figure derived from the catalog can be read with its limits.

unscored_techniques.why_unscored: NISS codes six metrics. Four of them (Biological Impact, Cognitive/Functional Disruption, Reversibility, Neuroplasticity) are claims about physical effect and persistence. These entries record the modality, its dual-use clinical counterpart and a physics feasibility tier, but not the effect, dose, persistence or access model, so those metrics cannot be coded from the entry without inventing evidence. Scoring them would produce numbers that look computed but are not.
unscored_techniques.what_would_change_this: Per technique: a cited measurement of the physical effect and its dose, a functional or clinical outcome mapping, an access and coupling model, and evidence on persistence. The sources already cited on each entry are the place to start.

requirements.name: Biological Impact
requirements.needs: A described physical or biological effect on tissue, with its magnitude or a cited measurement.

requirements.name: Cognitive Reconnaissance
requirements.needs: Whether the technique reads neural or cognitive content.

requirements.name: Cognitive/Functional Disruption
requirements.needs: A described disruption of cognition, perception, movement or autonomic function.

requirements.name: Consent Violation
requirements.needs: The access model: what proximity, equipment or authorisation an operator needs.

requirements.name: Reversibility
requirements.needs: Evidence of how long the effect persists and whether it resolves or is treatable.

requirements.name: Neuroplasticity
requirements.needs: Evidence of lasting structural or synaptic change, or of its absence.

missing_evidence.absent_means: The entry names the modality but not what it does to tissue at what dose.

missing_evidence.name: Cognitive/Functional Disruption
missing_evidence.needs: A described disruption of cognition, perception, movement or autonomic function.
missing_evidence.absent_means: No functional or clinical outcome mapping on the entry.

missing_evidence.name: Consent Violation
missing_evidence.needs: The access model: what proximity, equipment or authorisation an operator needs.
missing_evidence.absent_means: No access or coupling recorded, so the consent model cannot be derived.

missing_evidence.name: Reversibility
missing_evidence.needs: Evidence of how long the effect persists and whether it resolves or is treatable.
missing_evidence.absent_means: No persistence or drift evidence on the entry.

missing_evidence.name: Neuroplasticity
missing_evidence.needs: Evidence of lasting structural or synaptic change, or of its absence.
missing_evidence.absent_means: No evidence either way about lasting neural change.

severity_fields.issue: The catalog carries two severity answers that disagree. They are computed differently, over different populations, and are not interchangeable.

fields.source: Derived from the NISS vector by the scoring formula in niss_spec.
fields.authoritative_for: Any statement about neural impact severity. This is what the site displays.

fields.source: An original per-technique assessment that predates NISS scoring. No formula is recorded for it.
fields.authoritative_for: Nothing published. Retained because it is the only severity value the 26 unscored techniques carry.

severity_fields.known_conflict: No scored technique reaches NISS critical, while the legacy field marks some critical. The two are not comparable: the legacy field was not produced by the NISS formula.
severity_fields.resolution_status: Open framework decision: whether to retire the legacy field, rename it so it cannot be mistaken for a NISS score, or keep it as a separate recorded assessment.
